name: Ainu
notes: Research. Ainu (Hokkaido Ainu) is a language isolate, romanized in the Latin orthography standard in modern Ainu-language dictionaries and pedagogy (Tamura 1988, 2000; Refsing 1986). Beyond the plain Latin letters, ⟨sh⟩ spells /s/ (not s+h), ⟨ch⟩ spells the affricate /ts/ (not c+h), ⟨r⟩ is a tap [ɾ], and a doubled consonant letter (tt, nn, kk, ss, pp, mm) spells a geminate. Stress is predictable from syllable weight: falls on the second syllable if the first is open (light), otherwise on the first (closed/heavy) syllable (Tamura 1988); modelled here with a second-syllable default since the majority pattern in the sampled gold is disyllabic with an open first syllable. This entry was previously a structural-contact placeholder claiming no phonology; NorthEuraLex's `ain` gold sample confirmed the Latin romanization (rather than katakana, Ainu's other common script) matches this practical orthography, so the placeholder has been replaced with a real, cited grapheme map.
